name: James Talarico

issue_poll.name: University of Texas / Texas Politics Project poll (Aug 5-13, 2026, 1,200 registered voters), combined with Emerson College Texas poll (Oct 17-19, 2026) and Fox News Texas poll (Sept 24-28, 2026)
issue_poll.note: Base order from UT/TPP open-ended 'most important problem' facing the country and facing Texas (summed): inflation/prices 19%/19%, political corruption/leadership 17%/15%, economy 17%/10%, immigration 5%/10% plus border security 2%/4%, health care 4%/4%, energy/grid, utility rates and gas prices ~7% combined (Texas), Iran war 3%/1%. Emerson's final pre-election poll (economy 39%, immigration 16%, threats to democracy 13%, education 12%, health care 9%) used to add Democracy and elections and Education. Fox News Sept poll (cost of living 92% extremely/very important, immigration 79%, data centers 68%) used to add AI and data centers. 'Moral decline' (4%) and 'Trump' dropped as not vote-testable. Ranks 5-10 are approximate.

issues.detail: Repeal One Big Beautiful Bill tax breaks for top 1% to fund a cost-of-living tax cut; permanently expand child tax credit; universal child care; paid family leave.
Raise federal minimum wage above $15 (more than double $7.25); expand overtime pay; grants for entrepreneurs; citizen stake in U.S. AI companies.
Ban congressional stock trading; ban super PACs and corporate PAC contributions; congressional and Supreme Court term limits; ban presidential pardons.
Pathway to citizenship for long-term residents with back taxes, English, background check; more Border Patrol agents and surveillance technology; keep ICE but rein it in.
Nationwide ban on partisan gerrymandering; remove dark money from politics; expand voting access.
Public option: let Americans of any age buy into Medicare; cancel medical debt; protect Medicare and Medicaid.
Create universal pre-kindergarten; oppose federal school voucher programs; fully fund public schools.
Suspend the federal gas tax; fund and expand LIHEAP eligibility with fairer share for hot states; all-of-the-above energy incl. oil, gas, renewables.
Federal minimum standards for new data centers (grid, environment, jobs, transparency); large users pay own grid costs; closed-loop water required; local approval power.
End the war in Iran and Middle East 'forever wars'; no mechanism (funding cutoff, war powers vote) named.

plan_caveats: Issue ranking combines UT/TPP open-ended responses (Aug 2026) with Emerson (Oct) and Fox News (Sept) closed-list items; the polls use different questions, so ranks 5-10 are approximate. A UT/TPP Oct 10-12 poll found via Yahoo may be from 2025 and was not used.
Campaign issues page (jamestalarico.com/issues) could not be fetched; ratings rely on a campaign flyer PDF, OnTheIssues, and 2026 news coverage of plan releases and the CNN town hall.
Economy rated Concrete on minimum wage 'more than $15' (no exact figure); a stricter reading would be Partial on that item.
Some data center items (repeal Texas sales tax exemption, local approval) are state-level and not testable by Senate votes; Concrete rests on federal minimum standards and cost-causer grid pricing.
Education Concrete rests on universal pre-K (new program); voucher opposition is a 'no' position checkable only if a federal voucher bill comes up.
Iran rated Partial: 'end the war' stated, but no funding cutoff or war powers commitment found.
Also stated but outside the top 10: codify Roe v. Wade; end tariffs on everyday goods and farm inputs; national ban on gender surgeries for minors; first-time homebuyer down payment assistance.
Win as given in task (CBS News projection); not independently confirmed in this research.
